docs.description: Three voltages that swirl around each other and never repeat, from the Lorenz attractor: organic modulation for anything that should wander without looping. Changing a param bends the path rather than restarting it.

beta.description: β, the attractor's shape: 5 is β = 10, and the default is the classic β = 8/3

rate.description: simulation speed: 0 freezes and 5 is fastest; the default traces a slow butterfly, and from about 1.25 the chaos runs at audio rate

rho.description: ρ, how far the attractor's two lobes sit from the centre: 5 is ρ = 60, and the default is ρ = 28; below about 2.06 (ρ ≈ 24.74) the motion settles to a still point

sigma.description: σ, how fast x chases y: 5 is σ = 30, and the default is σ = 10; stays chaotic above 0

docs.description: The surface of a simulated sea as CV: slow rolls that bunch into sharp crests and arrive in sets, with the occasional wave far bigger than the rest. Use it for tidal filter sweeps and levels that breathe irregularly; `tilt` and `roll` are the matching lean of a boat on the water. Changing a param bends the waves rather than restarting them, and each channel is its own sea.

seed.description: picks the sea: each seed, and each channel, places the waves at different frequencies and directions

spread.description: directional spread: 0 sends every wave the same way, 5 brings them from every direction, a confused sea

AtomValue.description:
Atomic value types produced by the `$p()` DSL parser.

The reduced set from strudel's krill grammar: `Number` covers bare
numeric atoms, `Hz` covers frequency-tagged numbers (`440hz`), `Note`
covers pitched letter-octave atoms (`c4`, `d#3`, `eb5`), and `Truthy`
covers the `x` structure marker. Every other atom form (`m60` midi
shorthand, sample-name identifiers, `2v` voltage, module references,
quoted strings) has been removed from the grammar and is not
representable here.

oneOf.description:
Numeric value. Module-level semantics decide the interpretation:
`$cycle($p(...))` maps a bare `Number` to volts (1V/oct); `$p.s(...)`
maps it to an integer scale degree.

Structure atom `x` — an onset marker with no pitch of its own, only
meaningful in boolean (`.struct(...)`) patterns.

FactorPayload.description:

not a highlightable source. A parsed pattern (`.fast("2 4")`) becomes its own
highlightable source, so its active value lights up in the editor as it
drives the speed. A non-positive factor (`0` or negative) yields silence,
matching how the in-string `*`/`/` operators lower the same factors.
